factorRatings.note: Wallyhood's 2015 neighborhood write-up calls this longtime Wallingford pizza-and-pasta house 'comfortable with a capital C,' praising its Greek-inflected, garlicky pizza and genuinely friendly staff, though it notes Yelp reviews only reach 3 stars (mostly over wait times) and commenters were split, with one calling the dough noticeably sweet.

Seattle Weekly's 2012 review of this newly-opened Phinney Ridge spot praised a crust 'pillowy on the inside, crispy on the outside' under a generously-sauced pepperoni 'True Value' and locally-themed specialty pies; The Stranger separately highlighted its well-kept, family-friendly, arcade-equipped room named for neighborhood founder Guy Phinney.

A 2010 neighborhood-blog review ('Top shelf pizza at Pudge Bros') gave it 4.5 'licks of the lips,' praising a light, airy crust, a standout marinara balancing sweetness, mild spice and tomato flavor, and surprisingly attentive counter service at this tiny, no-frills NE 45th St. slice shop that deliberately skips elaborate topping combinations in favor of a strong base.
